To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the water structure in protein active sites can be classified as either favorable or unfavorable based on whether the water molecules are able to maintain favorable energetic contacts to both the surface and the surrounding water molecules.

the solvation enthalpy of protein active sites can be understood in terms of the enthalpic breakdown of water structure, and that the enthalpic penalty associated with this breakdown is often significant.

the water structure around the ligand-binding sites of six structurally diverse protein structures is highly variable, that water structure is highly dependent on the local surface topography and chemical nature, and that local water structure can be characterized in terms of the enthalpic breakdown of the hydrogen-bond network.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the thermodynamics of protein-ligand binding.

the enthalpic breakdown of water structure around protein active-site surfaces, with a view towards understanding the thermodynamic driving forces for protein-ligand binding and the role of water in this process.
the thermodynamics of water reorganization around proteins, with particular emphasis on the thermodynamics of the displacement of water molecules from protein active sites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the solvation enthalpies of protein active-site surfaces are a complex function of the local surface topology and the local water structure.

the enthalpic breakdown of water structure is not only a function of surface topography, but also a function of the chemical nature of the surface, and that the enthalpy of water reorganization is a complex and dynamic process.
water is not structured in the active-site pockets of proteins, but that water molecules are structured around individual atoms and groups in the pockets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we find the enthalpy of hydration of water molecules on protein active-site surfaces to be a function of the geometry of the surface as well as the chemical nature of the surface, and that these two factors can lead to a breakdown of the water structure in a way that is energetically unfavorable relative to bulk.
water structure on protein surfaces is highly variable and that this variation is not well described by the simple hydrophobic effect.

the water structure on a protein surface can be characterized in terms of the energetic interactions between water molecules and the surface, the interactions between neighboring water molecule pairs, the energetic cost of displacing water, and the energetic cost of forming a water molecule.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no simple correlation between local water structure and the overall enthalpy of solvation.
the enthalpic penalty for water displacement from a surface is not necessarily correlated to the overall enthalpy of the solvation of that surface.

there are certain topographies on protein surfaces that are not amenable to solvation by water molecules, which may be a factor contributing to the enthalpy of binding of small molecules to these sites.
